LESSON: ACTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Listening and Speaking Active listening Attentive listening, pronunciation, comp
Topic 1.1: Active Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Active Listening, part of Listening and Speaking Active listening Attentive listening, pronunciation, comp in Grade 6 MANDARIN.

Key inquiry question: How can you minimise distractions while listening?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen and repeat saying the Chinese personal pronouns (我、你、您、他、她) in turns,

2. listen to a recording about greetings for different moments of the day (早上好、上午 好、中午好、下午好、晚上好、晚安) and repeat after it,

3. sing the Chinese numbers song (1-50) with peers,

4. listen and repeat saying a Chinese tongue- twister on numbers in turns (四是四,十是 十,十四是十四,四不是十,十不是四) with the correct pronunciation ,

5. take turns introducing themselves and their friends, (name and age) (e.g. 你/您好、早上好

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen and repeat saying the Chinese personal pronouns (我、你、您、他、她) in turns,
2. listen to a recording about greetings for different moments of the day (早上好、上午 好、中午好、下午好、晚上好、晚安) and repeat after it,
3. sing the Chinese numbers song (1-50) with peers,
4. listen and repeat saying a Chinese tongue- twister on numbers in turns (四是四,十是 十,十四是十四,四不是十,十不是四) with the correct pronunciation ,
5. take turns introducing themselves and their friends, (name and age) (e.g. 你/您好、早上好

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Active Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: The learner speaks effectively and logically when they introduce themselves and their

friends.

Values:
Unity: The learner displays team spirit when they recite the Chinese tongue twister on numbers with their peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion is strengthened as the learner exhibits the commonly held norms and values that promote acceptance in the

community when they introduce themselves and others appropriately.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner can relate their learning to English and Kiswahili on the concept of conveying their thoughts and ideas clearly using

appropriate pronunciation.
